data.narrative:
Cartesia is a Series B-stage AI & Software company that has raised $186M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-sector, same-stage private comparables (Physical Intelligence at $5.6B, Black Forest Labs at $3.2B, and Field AI at $2.0B), supplemented by reference to public software and AI infrastructure companies including Palantir.

Two valuation methods are applicable here. Stage-progression methodology, using total capital raised as a proxy base and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage step-ups, implies a valuation of $353M. Peer-median valuation, based on the three same-stage AI & Software comparables, yields a median of $3.2B with a range spanning $2.0B to $5.6B. The wide dispersion in the peer set reflects heterogeneity in model stage, commercial traction, and capital efficiency within frontier AI.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $300M (floor, stage-progression conservative) to $3.7B (ceiling, peer-high bound), with a median implied value of $1.8B. Key uncertainties include: the relevance of stage-progression given Cartesia's likely differentiated burn profile within frontier AI; materiality of revenue or usage metrics not captured in the peer set; and timing and terms of the next fundraise round. The gap between stage-progression and peer-median estimates suggests material downside/upside depending on commercial execution relative to peer benchmark.
